title: Proving What Marketing Actually Works: A Geo Holdout Test for Social Ads
excerpt: Attribution tools tell you which ads got clicked. They don't tell you which ads actually changed someone's behaviour. Here's how I designed a geo holdout experiment to measure the true, causal contribution of a social advertising channel — and why the answer surprised everyone.

title: How Much of Paid Search Is Just Buying Clicks You'd Get for Free?
excerpt: Paid search is the channel everyone trusts and nobody questions. So I ran a holdout test that asked an uncomfortable question — when we pause paid search, how much of that traffic just comes back through organic for free? The answer reshaped how the budget was allocated.

title: Two Roads to a Valid Control Group: Zip-Level Incrementality for Programmatic Ads
excerpt: When you test a programmatic channel at the zip-code level, the entire experiment lives or dies on one thing: is your control group a real twin of your treatment? I ran two tests where the data situations were completely different — and each demanded a completely different way of building that twin.
